history.text: The guard sees two men come from St Brendan's and checks the building plan for an entrance that could explain them.
That door only opens out.
One man is dragging the other clear of the west doors. Neither has a postcard, guidebook or receipt.
The second man gives the name already waiting in the RETURNED column.
I kept the line.
The demolition order is still clipped under the ledger. It does not happen in this account.
The guard writes WEST DOORS beside both signatures.
Later, somebody adds EXIT THROUGH THE GIFT SHOP in another hand and leaves both names alone.
There's another recording. Listen to what comes before the notes.

line.text: The guard listens to the chair scrape, the two notes and the machine being set down. He writes RECORDING RETAINED beside the two signatures.

history.text: The first bell finds the crossing. The second finds the Surfer.
By the third, the distinction between the two available bodies has become an acoustic problem.
That is what they were for.
Four. The screen answers at the same distance as the screen in Ellery Chapel, though nobody here measures it.
Five. Cold glass gives back the same chord from another building and refuses to explain the correspondence.
Six takes your voice. Seven sets both bodies on the same step.
Eight completes the return through both of you. The bell mouths do not move.
No porch opens. No chapel inherits the run. The demolition remains paperwork for a morning that belongs to another route.
